msg: Hola, buen día. Somos un grupo de 7 amigas de Bogotá. Tres ya tenemos el Open Water, dos quieren probar el minicurso y dos prefieren snorkel. ¿Cuánto saldría por persona saliendo desde Cartagena y hay descuento por grupo?
reply:
¡Hola! 🪸 Soy *Coral*, de *Diving Planet* — buceamos todo el año en las Islas del Rosario, saliendo desde Cartagena o desde las propias islas. 🌊

¡Buen día! ¡Qué chévere plan para las siete! Sí, pueden combinar buceo para certificadas, minicurso y snorkel en la misma salida; el snorkel se realiza en una zona distinta a la del buceo.

Te dejo a continuación los precios por persona desde Cartagena para cada actividad. Para el grupo aplica un 10% de descuento adicional al 10% online en minicurso y snorkel; deben solicitarlo al equipo antes de pagar. No aplica a cursos PADI.

*Precios por persona* (online · normal):
*Desde Cartagena* — lancha desde el Muelle de la Bodeguita · con almuerzo
• Minicurso de Buceo: 655.000 COP · 727.000 COP
• Tour de Snorkeling: 448.000 COP · 497.000 COP
*Ya en las Islas del Rosario* — recogida en tu hotel si tiene acceso por lancha · sin almuerzo
• Minicurso de Buceo: 475.000 COP · 528.000 COP
• Tour de Snorkeling: 150.000 COP · 167.000 COP

No hay descuento ni tarifa especial por ser colombiano: el precio es el mismo, solo cambia la moneda (COP).

Entonces, ¿saldrías *desde Cartagena* (Muelle de la Bodeguita)? 🚤

The mini course dive ends around 12:00 (noon): its 12 hours count from then. If the last dive is a daytime one, the refresher's included (activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day; after the mini-course, from midnight that same day. If the last dive is a night dive, the hours count from it. A flight the next day at 7:00 a.m. or later IS fine: they can dive the day before, and that day's return time to Cartagena changes nothing. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.
- If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.

- Muelle de la Bodeguita, 5 minutes from the historic center, at 8:00 AM. Departing from Cartagena there is no hotel pick-up: each person gets to the dock on their own (ground transportation to the dock is not included).

- Date changes are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/

Saying they are Colombian or from a Colombian city ("I'm from Cali") already says it; what is not enough is only having been born there while living abroad: then ask whether they hold Colombian nationality or a cédula de extranjería. All other international clients pay in US dollars (USD). A group does not pay in parts: if the same booking mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group pays in US dollars (USD), residents and Colombians included. A Colombian together with someone who holds a cédula de extranjería, wherever they are from, is not a mixed group: both pay in pesos (COP). The price is the same: only the currency changes (there is no discount for being Colombian).

msg: Solo yo. ¿A qué hora me recogerían en el Cocoliso y tengo que llevar algo? Gracias.
reply:
En Cocoliso te recogerían entre las 9:30 y las 9:45 a. m. y regresarías al hotel hacia las 12:00–1:00 p. m. Lleva tu carné de buceo, bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo está incluido. Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresher; y recuerda esperar al menos 18 horas después de bucear antes de tomar un vuelo.

También necesitas:
• Estar listo a las 9:30 en tu hotel
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.

¿Han pasado *más de 2 años* desde tu última inmersión?

msg: Hi there! We're a family from Canada staying in Cartagena next month. My wife and I are both Advanced Open Water divers, and we have two kids, aged 11 and 7. What could each of us do on a day trip from Cartagena, and how much would it cost?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

That sounds like a lovely family day in the Rosario Islands! 🌊

- **You and your wife:** As certified divers, you can each join the **Fun Dives trip** with two guided reef dives. It’s a same-day trip from Cartagena, with boat transport and lunch included. - **Your 11-year-old:** Options include snorkeling or the Dive Mini Course. The mini-course includes pool practice and one ocean dive with an instructor. The minimum age for certified fun dives is 10, but those require Open Water certification. - **Your 7-year-old:** Can join the snorkeling tour and enjoy the reef from the surface. Bubble Makers starts at age 8.

For the certified divers, the day trip requires at least two dives from Cartagena. The prices for the other options are listed below.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• Fun Dives - 2 dives (1 day): 178 USD · 197 USD
• 3-dive package (1 day, 2 daytime + 1 night dive): 287 USD · 319 USD
• 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives): 316 USD · 351 USD

Would you like the booking links for the activities that can be booked online?

• *Come along as a companion* — Comes on the boat and enjoys the day with the group, without getting in the water.

msg: Good afternoon. I am from Germany and I hold an Open Water certification, although I have not dived for three years. I am staying in Getsemaní and I would like to dive next Wednesday. My flight home leaves on Thursday at 22:00. Is this possible, and what would you recommend?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Good afternoon! Since you’re certified and haven’t dived for three years, the recommended option is a **refresher**. It includes a daytime dive, and you can fly from **7:00 a.m. the following day** after that dive. So a Thursday flight at 22:00 works with a Wednesday refresher.

The trip departs at 8:00 a.m. from Muelle de la Bodeguita and returns to Cartagena around 4:15 p.m. You’ll need to show your certified diver card.

Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers).

You can choose Wednesday and the number of participants here: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/minicurso-de-buceo/2?language=en

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

There is always availability: we operate every day, including public holidays, except December 25 and January 1; if sea conditions are not safe, the trip is rescheduled.

How many people would this be for: just you, or more? 😊

msg: Good, thank you. Two last questions: do you pick me up in Getsemaní or how do I reach the dock, and do I have to bring my certification card or fill in any forms for these two days?
reply:
There’s no hotel pick-up in Getsemaní. Please make your own way to **Muelle de la Bodeguita** for the **8:00 a.m.** departure. It’s about five minutes from the historic center; at entrance 3, ask for **DIVING PLANET**. Ground transport to the dock isn’t included. [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Muelle+de+la+Bodeguita/@10.4199447,-75.5537609,828m/data=!3m2!1e3!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x8ef62f753729822d:0x1bbcdd8224d0eaaf!8m2!3d10.4199447!4d-75.551186!16s%2Fg%2F113gzkckf?entry=ttu)

Bring your **certification card**—you can show it on the day or send a photo beforehand. For the **refresher**, complete the course medical form: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. There’s no theory to do beforehand; you’ll do it with the instructor on the day. For the two-dive trip, complete the insurance form from your booking confirmation email and the certified-diver liability waiver: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol. The forms are in Spanish; if you haven’t completed the insurance form, it will be sent again in the confirmation email.

You'll also need:
• If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.
• After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying
• Minimum age: 10 and over.
• For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.
• What to bring: swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving or snorkeling gear is included in dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and PADI courses; the Divemaster uses their own gear.

msg: Gracias. Nos interesa el minicurso, para los dos. ¿A qué profundidad se baja? Y mi esposa pregunta si hace falta saber nadar muy bien, porque ella nada lo justo. Quisiéramos ir el sábado 14 de noviembre.
reply:
El minicurso llega hasta **12 metros**; lo habitual es bucear entre 5 y 12 metros. La inmersión se hace con instructor, después de la teoría y la práctica en piscina.

Sobre saber nadar: no tengo ese requisito específico confirmado. Como tu esposa nada lo justo y tiene poca confianza en el agua, es importante que lo comente con un asesor antes de reservar para que pueda orientarlos con seguridad. El sábado 14 de noviembre es la fecha que desean; la disponibilidad de ese día la confirma el equipo.

También necesitas:
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 12 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.

🤿 *Minicurso de Buceo*
💰 *655.000 COP* por persona · 2 personas

El pago es en pesos colombianos (COP): pueden pagar *100 % online* o un *anticipo del 50 %* con el enlace, el QR o Llave que envía el asesor, y el *otro 50 % el día de la actividad*.

msg: Hola, buenos días. Soy Diana, de Bogotá. Quiero sacarme la certificación de buceo y he pensado hacerlo en Cartagena en enero. Tengo asma leve, controlada con inhalador, y hace años que no tengo una crisis. ¿Puedo hacer el curso igual? ¿Cuánto dura y cuánto cuesta?
reply:
El Curso Open Water dura 2 días. Saliendo desde Cartagena, el precio es **2.450.000 COP online** o **2.722.000 COP normal**.

El curso requiere alojarse al menos una noche en las islas; el alojamiento no está incluido. El día 1 empieza a las 8:00 a. m. en el Muelle de la Bodeguita y el regreso a Cartagena es el día 2, aproximadamente a las 4:15 p. m.

Para preguntas médicas específicas, es importante que hables con nuestro staff calificado para evaluar tu situación particular. Te paso ahora con alguien del equipo, que te escribe por aquí enseguida.

msg: Perfecto, gracias, espero entonces lo del asma. Mientras tanto, otra duda: tengo que estar en Bogotá el lunes para trabajar. Si hago el curso sábado y domingo, ¿puedo coger un vuelo el domingo por la noche, cuando vuelva a Cartagena? Y sobre la teoría, ¿tengo que estudiar algo antes de ir?
reply:
Para el Curso Open Water, debes esperar al menos 18 horas desde tu última inmersión antes de volar. Así que un vuelo el domingo por la noche no sería posible; que la lancha regrese a Cartagena ese día no cambia ese tiempo.

Sí, debes completar antes la teoría de PADI eLearning, que toma aproximadamente 10 a 12 horas. El asesor ya tiene tu caso sobre el asma y te escribirá por aquí.

También necesitas:
• Con este plan debes alojarte al menos 1 noche en las Islas del Rosario (hotel no incluido)
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.

Para preguntas médicas específicas, es importante que hables con nuestro staff calificado para evaluar tu situación particular. Te paso ahora con alguien del equipo, que te escribe por aquí enseguida.

msg: Hey! Planning a bachelor party in Cartagena in February, there will be 6 of us from Texas. Three of the guys are certified and three have never dived. We want one day out on the water together. What's the deal price-wise for a group like ours? And can we pay with US credit cards? One of us would pay for everybody.
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

That sounds like a great bachelor-party day on the water! The three certified divers can book the one-day, two-dive Fun Dives. The three who haven’t dived before can choose a Dive Mini Course, snorkeling, or come along as companions. The mini-course is an introduction, not a certification, so it doesn’t let them join the certified dives.

For the group discount, your group qualifies for an extra 10% on eligible activities, on top of the 10% online discount. It isn’t applied automatically, so it must be requested before paying; it applies to recreational diving, mini-courses, snorkeling, and the companion plan, but not PADI courses. I’m leaving the prices below.

International guests can pay by card on the website, and one person can pay for the booking. The booking is paid in full online; with a foreign card, use a passport as the ID document. Here are the separate booking links for the certified dives and the mini-course:

- [Fun Dives — 2 dives](https://book.divingplanet.org/book/salidas-de-buceo/1?language=en)
- [Dive Mini Course](https://book.divingplanet.org/book/minicurso-de-buceo/2?language=en)

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• Fun Dives - 2 dives (1 day): 178 USD · 197 USD
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

Guests who are not Colombian or residents of Colombia pay in US dollars (USD) by card on the website; the rate is the same, only the currency changes.

Would you like to include snorkeling or companion spots for anyone who prefers not to dive?

msg: Good call on asking: one of the certified guys, Mike, last dived about three years ago. The other two dived last summer. No beers, got it. So what does Mike need to do? And who do I talk to on your team to get the group discount before we pay?
reply:
Since Mike last dived about three years ago, he’ll normally need a refresher before joining the certified dives. It’s a pool session and one dive with an instructor, and it takes a separate day—he can’t do the refresher and the dive trip on the same day. If he has already completed a refresher or PADI ReActivate at another center, that counts. Very experienced divers with 500+ dives or Dive Master level can be reviewed by a team advisor.

To request the group discount, contact a team advisor **before paying**. The 10% group discount applies to your recreational dives and mini-courses, and stacks with the 10% online discount. It isn’t automatic and can’t be added after payment. Would you like me to connect you with a team advisor?

You'll also need:
• There is no theory to do beforehand: it is done there, on the day, with the instructor.
• The medical form is required for courses or mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). The link can be sent together with the booking link; if you have not completed it, it is sent again in the booking confirmation email. Exception: the refresher (a review with an instructor) uses the course medical form, even if you are a certified diver.
• To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.
• After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying
• Minimum age: 10 and over.
• What to bring: swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving or snorkeling gear is included in dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and PADI courses; the Divemaster uses their own gear.
• After diving, wait at least 12 hours before flying

Keep in mind that the mini-course is a one-day introduction and does not certify you; to get certified there is the Open Water course (2 days, with a night on the islands).

msg: Good afternoon. My name is Anna, I am from Germany. I will stay at the Hotel San Pedro de Majagua on Isla Grande from November 20 to 24. I am a PADI Advanced diver with about 80 dives, my last dive was in September in Egypt. How does it work when I am already on the island: do you pick me up at the hotel, and what does it cost? I would like to dive on two of the days.
reply:
Hi, Anna! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Good afternoon, Anna! Diving on two days from Isla Grande is a lovely way to explore the reefs, and your Advanced certification is suitable for the certified-diving options.

Yes—San Pedro de Majagua is one of our base hotels, so pick-up and return by boat are included at no extra charge. For the two-day, four-daytime-dive package, pick-up is between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. on each day; you’ll return to the hotel around 12:00–1:00 p.m. Lunch isn’t included for island-based plans.

I’m leaving the prices below.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives): 204 USD · 227 USD
• Fun Dives - 2 dives (1 day): 124 USD · 138 USD
• 4-dive package (2 days, 3 daytime + 1 night dive): 236 USD · 262 USD
• 5-dive package (2 days): 319 USD · 354 USD

From the islands we coordinate pick-up and drop-off at your hotel if it has maritime access, or at the nearest dock we point you to.

Would you prefer four daytime dives, or would you like to include a night dive?

Diving Planet policies:
- Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers). The refresher is also 18 hours: it is for certified divers, even though it is booked as the mini course. The hours count from the last dive, not from the return to Cartagena. The mini course dive ends around 12:00 (noon): its 12 hours count from then. If the last dive is a daytime one, the refresher's included (activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day; after the mini-course, from midnight that same day. If the last dive is a night dive, the hours count from it. A flight the next day at 7:00 a.m. or later IS fine: they can dive the day before, and that day's return time to Cartagena changes nothing. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.
- If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.
- For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.
- Muelle de la Bodeguita, 5 minutes from the historic center, at 8:00 AM. Departing from Cartagena there is no hotel pick-up: each person gets to the dock on their own (ground transportation to the dock is not included).
- By booking you accept our terms and conditions, cancellation policy, and data treatment. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Date changes are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Changes to the number of people on a booking you already made are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Colombians (anyone with Colombian nationality, holding a Colombian cédula or passport, wherever they live; also dual nationals when one nationality is Colombian) and residents of Colombia (holders of a cédula de extranjería, a resident ID; living in Colombia without one is not enough) pay in Colombian pesos (COP). Saying they are Colombian or from a Colombian city ("I'm from Cali") already says it; what is not enough is only having been born there while living abroad: then ask whether they hold Colombian nationality or a cédula de extranjería. All other international clients pay in US dollars (USD). A group does not pay in parts: if the same booking mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group pays in US dollars (USD), residents and Colombians included. A Colombian together with someone who holds a cédula de extranjería, wherever they are from, is not a mixed group: both pay in pesos (COP). The price is the same: only the currency changes (there is no discount for being Colombian).
- If the group mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group booking is paid in US dollars (USD), at the same equivalent price. Someone with a cédula de extranjería does not count as a foreigner, wherever they are from. There is no different price for being Colombian.
- If you are already on the Rosario Islands, we coordinate pick-up and drop-off from hotels with maritime access. In some cases the boat arrives directly at the hotel; in others we indicate the nearest dock or meeting point.
- These plans have different prices because they do not include transport from Cartagena or lunch.
- Pick-up is only on the Rosario Islands: Barú (including Playa Blanca, which is on Barú) is not part of the islands and we do not operate or pick up there; guests staying in Barú depart from Cartagena (Muelle de la Bodeguita).
- It depends on the activity: snorkeling from 6 years old; Bubble Makers from 8 to 10 years old (pool mini-course and very shallow water practice, max 2 meters); the dive mini-course and the Open Water course from 10 years old; the Advanced course and the Rescue course from 12. Minors must be accompanied by a demonstrable parent or responsible relative.
- The medical form is required for courses or mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). The link can be sent together with the booking link; if you have not completed it, it is sent again in the booking confirmation email. Exception: the refresher (a review with an instructor) uses the course medical form, even if you are a certified diver.
- If you are a certified diver, there are no additional medical restrictions; your liability waiver is the certified-diver one: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). For the refresher day this one is not used: use the course medical form.
- Bringing or drinking alcohol on the boat or during the activity is not allowed, and no alcohol or other substances may be consumed before diving. You must be in good physical condition.
- The booking system on our website. It automatically closes at 4:30 PM the day before: after that time you can no longer book for the next day, and you still book on the website for the next available day.
- To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.

Daytime activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m. (see the activity schedule). Night diving: in the evening (pick-up around 5:30 p.m., back around 7:30 p.m.). Online booking system closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before; after that, you book on the website for the next available day.
- We only close on December 25 and January 1. The rest of the year we operate every day, including public holidays, except for suspension due to adverse weather conditions.

Vegetarians, vegans, and celiacs receive rice with vegetables. Guests may bring their own food if needed (e.g. allergy or special diet). If the guest has a food allergy, they must inform us before the tour. In multi-day packages departing from Cartagena, lunch is included on the first day only; plans for guests already on the islands do not include lunch.
- Photos and videos are not offered proactively or included in the price. The instructor may take them voluntarily and delivers them by the next day at the latest. Any tip to the instructor for photos/videos is voluntary: each guest gives whatever they like, directly to them. This applies to every activity, including the mini-course (and the refresher, booked as a mini-course), PADI courses and certified-diver trips: not included, the instructor may take them voluntarily.
- The 3, 4, 5, 7 and 9 dive packages are exclusively for certified divers with a minimum Open Water level. They are not available for uncertified beginners.
- Two-day courses (Open Water, Referral Course, Advanced, Rescue and Mindful Diving) require accommodation on the islands: at least one night, the night of day 1 (there is no return to Cartagena on day 1). There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel. The same goes for multi-day dive packages (4, 5, 7 and 9 dives): you stay on the islands, and accommodation, which is not included, is booked directly with the hotel.
- Private services and closed groups are available, with no fixed price (it depends on the group and the date). A member of our team prepares the quote and coordinates an available instructor for the date.
- Through DIVE TO HEAL, more than 360 people with disabilities have been served. Accepted conditions include: hearing impairment (deaf), visual impairment (blind), reduced mobility (wheelchair), Down Syndrome, Cerebral Palsy, and Autism (depending on level and assessment). All instructors are trained in adaptive diving. Advance notice is recommended. The limitation is the presence of additional medical conditions that contraindicate diving.
- If you're already on the Rosario Islands and your hotel has maritime access, boat pick-up and drop-off are included at no extra charge.
- We dive in the Rosario Islands, inside the Corales del Rosario y San Bernardo National Natural Park, about 45-60 minutes by boat from Cartagena.
- All daytime activities (dive trips, mini-course, snorkeling, courses and each day of the packages) end around 12:00-1:00 p.m., followed by lunch. Guests departing from Cartagena have lunch included on the islands and the boat returns to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.); guests staying on the islands return to their hotel around 12:00-1:00 p.m. for lunch (lunch not included). On overnight courses and packages, day 1's daytime activities also end around 12:00-1:00 p.m., and then you go to your hotel on the islands. Night diving (on plans that include it) is separate, in the evening (see each plan's schedule).

- There is no minimum number of people: every activity runs even for a single person.
- Activities and courses are taught in Spanish and English. If a participant speaks neither language, they can come with someone who interprets for them, but instruction is still given in Spanish or English.

Answer: Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers). For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. Question: Are fish, sharks, starfish, coral, or sea urchins dangerous?
Other ways to ask: Is it dangerous to encounter sharks, fish, or sea urchins while diving? / Should I be concerned about marine animals like coral or starfish when diving?
Answer: Most fish avoid humans. If you see a shark, the recommended approach is to stay calm, observe, and enjoy the moment from a respectful distance; encounters are usually safe. Touching starfish, turtles, coral, or any organism is not recommended: many are delicate or sensitive. Many minor diving injuries occur from accidental contact with coral or sea urchins, which is why neutral buoyancy and not touching anything are fundamental for safety.

msg: Hiya! I'm Priya, a British backpacker on a tight budget, currently in Santa Marta and heading to Cartagena next week. I've got three free days, November 17 to 19, and I've always wanted to get my diving certification. Is that doable in three days, and what's the cheapest way of doing it? I've got a hostel in Getsemaní booked already.
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

That’s a lovely goal, Priya—the Rosario Islands are a beautiful place to earn your first certification. Yes, the PADI Open Water course can fit within your three free days: the course itself takes two days, but you’ll need to stay overnight on the islands after day one. Your Getsemaní hostel won’t cover that overnight stay, and accommodation on the islands isn’t included.

The course includes online theory, pool sessions and four certification dives. From Cartagena, you meet at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. on day one; the return to Cartagena on day two is around 4:15 p.m. The online price is the cheapest listed option, and I’m leaving the prices below.

• PADI Basic Course (Open Water): 693 USD · 770 USD

msg: Brilliant. How long does the online theory take, and when do I get access to it? I'd have about a week to do it. Also, I need somewhere cheap to sleep on the island for that one night: do you know a budget option? And would I save anything by going to the island the day before and starting from there?
reply:
The Open Water online theory takes about **10–12 hours** and must be completed before the practical sessions. The course information says access is through PADI eLearning, but doesn’t specify exactly when access is issued. Having a week sounds like a good window to complete it.

Accommodation isn’t included, and you’ll need to book directly with a hotel on the islands for the night after day one. I don’t have budget rates to compare, but nearby options with maritime access include Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras and Pao Pao.

The course price is the same whether you start from Cartagena or are already on the islands, so going out the day before doesn’t reduce the course price. The Cartagena course includes round-trip boat transport; the island-based course doesn’t include transport from Cartagena. You’d still need to arrange and pay for your own trip to the islands and accommodation.

How many people would this be for: just you, or more? 😊

msg: Okay, thanks. So who can tell me about the GoPro? I'd really like to film my first dives, it's kind of the whole point for me. And is storing my backpack at your office free? Last thing: I've got a flight to Medellín on the 19th at 9 in the morning, is that fine if I finish the course on the 18th?
reply:
You can bring your GoPro on the dives at your own risk. We don’t rent cameras, and underwater photos or videos aren’t included in the course. An instructor may take photos or videos as a voluntary gesture, but that isn’t guaranteed.

You can bring one backpack on the boat, so you shouldn’t need to store it at our Cartagena office. I don’t have information on whether office storage is free.

For your flight: after the Open Water course, you must wait at least **18 hours from your last dive**. The course’s final dives are on November 18, so a 9:00 a.m. flight on November 19 would be too soon. You’d need to move the flight to at least 18 hours after your last dive.

- Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers). If the last dive is a daytime one, the refresher's included (activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day; after the mini-course, from midnight that same day. If the last dive is a night dive, the hours count from it. A flight the next day at 7:00 a.m. or later IS fine: they can dive the day before, and that day's return time to Cartagena changes nothing. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.

If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. - Date changes are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Changes to the number of people on a booking you already made are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Colombians (anyone with Colombian nationality, holding a Colombian cédula or passport, wherever they live; also dual nationals when one nationality is Colombian) and residents of Colombia (holders of a cédula de extranjería, a resident ID; living in Colombia without one is not enough) pay in Colombian pesos (COP). Saying they are Colombian or from a Colombian city ("I'm from Cali") already says it; what is not enough is only having been born there while living abroad: then ask whether they hold Colombian nationality or a cédula de extranjería. All other international clients pay in US dollars (USD). A group does not pay in parts: if the same booking mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group pays in US dollars (USD), residents and Colombians included. The price is the same: only the currency changes (there is no discount for being Colombian).
- If the group mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group booking is paid in US dollars (USD), at the same equivalent price. Someone with a cédula de extranjería does not count as a foreigner, wherever they are from. There is no different price for being Colombian.

msg: tengo el advanced, necesito refresh?
reply:
Sí. Como llevas unos 4 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresh, aunque tengas Advanced. Es un repaso en piscina y una inmersión con instructor, y ocupa un día; ese mismo día no se hace otra salida de buceo. Si ya hiciste un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como tu refresh. 🪸

También necesitas:
• No hay teoría que hacer antes: se hace allí, el mismo día, con el instructor.
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 18 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.

¿Te animas con la *salida de 2 inmersiones*, un *paquete de varios días* o un *curso avanzado*? 🌊
